h1: The 7 Best 85 and 86-Inch TVs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 7 best 85 and 86-inch TVs of 2026, from Samsung and Hisense to LG Nano, commercial 86 inch sets and an outdoor model.
summary: The Hisense 85E6QF is the best large TV here, the only QLED set in the group. Samsung's U8000H is the safe brand choice, and the LG Nano model adds AI Sound Pro audio. For true 86 inch screens, LG's commercial panels fit offices, while the Phonecessity covers partial-sun patios.
intro: Shopping for an 86 inch TV is a little like shopping for a size that barely exists. Mainstream retail sells 85 inch sets, and the true 86 inch panels are mostly commercial signage or specialty outdoor models. The difference between the two sizes is about one inch, which no one sitting on a couch will ever notice.

We ranked seven sets that fit this size class. Four are consumer 85 inch TVs, two are commercial 86 inch panels and one is a weatherproof outdoor model. A 75 inch set was left out because it does not match. Each is scored on panel tier, features, intended use and who it actually suits.

products.name: Hisense 85" E6 Cinema Series Hi-QLED 4K UHD Smart Fire TV (85E6QF)
products.verdict: The only 85 inch QLED set in this ranking.
products.description:
The Hisense E6 Cinema Series is an 85 inch Hi-QLED 4K UHD smart TV running Fire TV, in the $500+ bracket. It is the only QLED panel among the seven.

It ranks first because the panel is a step above the plain LED and Crystal sets below it. QLED adds quantum dot color technology, which gives the picture more vivid color than a basic 4K display. The Samsung U8000H is a more familiar name, but its Crystal UHD panel sits lower on the technology ladder, so the Hisense gets the edge in a ranking built around picture class.

Buy it for a living-room cinema on a big wall. The caveat is a short spec list, so check refresh rate, HDMI ports and gaming features on the listing before you commit. If you need a genuine 86 inch panel, this is not it.
products.idealFor: Living-room cinema on a big wall.
products.skipIf: You need a true 86 inch panel.

products.name: Samsung 85-Inch Class U8000H Series Crystal UHD
products.description:
Samsung's U8000H is an 85 inch Crystal UHD 4K set in the $500+ bracket. It is the most recognized brand name in the group and keeps its feature list simple.

It ranks second because it trails the Hisense on panel technology. Crystal UHD is the entry tier of Samsung's lineup, with no QLED or Mini-LED listed. What it does offer is brand familiarity and a plain, dependable set for everyday television. It edges past the LG Nano model because that one asks you to judge audio processing, while the Samsung is just a straightforward big-screen 4K.

Buy it for general viewing from a name you trust. The caveat is that you are paying premium-bracket money for an entry panel, so a buyer who cares about picture should look at the Hisense first.
products.idealFor: General viewing from a trusted brand.

products.name: LG 85-Inch Class Nano AI 4K NU85 Series Smart TV w/AI Sound Pro
products.verdict: Nano panel plus AI Sound Pro audio processing.
products.description:
The LG Nano AI NU85 is an 85 inch 4K smart TV with AI Sound Pro, in the $500+ bracket. Its audio processing is the feature no other set in the group advertises.

It lands third because the Nano label sits below QLED in panel tier, and the Samsung beats it on name recognition for many shoppers. Where it pulls ahead is sound. Built-in speakers on slim TVs are often thin, and any software help with dialogue and bass is welcome in a living room without a soundbar.

Buy it if you watch a lot of movies and want better audio without extra gear. The caveat is that AI Sound Pro is processing, not a replacement for a real sound system, and the panel remains a modest tier. Hisense gives you a better screen.
products.idealFor: Viewers who want better built-in sound.

products.name: INSIGNIA 85" Class F50 Series LED 4K UHD Smart Fire TV with Alexa
products.verdict: Fire TV and Alexa built into a big 4K screen.
products.description:
Insignia's F50 is an 85 inch LED 4K UHD smart TV with Fire TV and Alexa voice control built in, in the $500+ bracket.

It sits fourth because the panel is the plain LED type, with no QLED, Nano or similar step up listed. The Samsung and LG sets above it offer more established panel names, and the Hisense runs the same Fire TV platform with a better screen. What the Insignia gives you is the simplest voice-first experience in the group, since Alexa is part of the package.

Buy it if you already live in the Alexa world and want a large screen to control by voice. Skip it if picture quality tops your list, since the listing names no advanced panel technology. This is a convenient set rather than an impressive one.
products.idealFor: Voice-control fans on a larger screen.

products.name: LG Commercial Lite 86UR340C9UD 86" Smart LED-LCD TV - 4K UHDTV - Navy
products.verdict: A real 86 inch commercial panel at the lowest cost here.
products.description:
The LG Commercial Lite 86UR340C9UD is a true 86 inch smart LED-LCD 4K panel in navy, in the $500+ bracket. It is the one real 86 inch set here that is priced like a mainstream option.

It ranks fifth because commercial sets are built for signage and meeting rooms, not living rooms. Fewer home features means less polish for gaming or streaming apps than on the consumer models above it. Yet it holds its place over the PK340S because it lists smart TV functions and carries the lowest cost among the 86 inch panels.

Buy it if you need exactly 86 inches, say for an office, a showroom or a basement with a measured wall. Skip it if you want consumer gaming features or the best possible picture, because the 85 inch consumer TVs are a better fit.

products.name: LG PK340S 86" UHD 4K HDR Commercial TV
products.verdict: An 86 inch commercial set with HDR.
products.description:
The LG PK340S is an 86 inch UHD 4K HDR commercial TV in the $500+ bracket. HDR support and a commercial build are its two selling points.

It ranks sixth because the listing is aimed at installers, not home viewers. Consumer details are thin, and it lacks the smart platform description that the cheaper LG Commercial Lite carries. Even with HDR, a commercial display is designed around uptime and mounting in public spaces rather than cinema picture.

Buy it for lobbies, classrooms and meeting rooms where the screen runs for hours and an 86 inch panel is a must. Skip it for a home theater. The caveat is that this is not a living-room product, and you would be better served by the Hisense or Samsung in a house.

products.name: Phonecessity Weatherproof Outdoor Partial Sun 86" 4K QNED Smart TV L-100 Powered
products.verdict: The only weatherproof 86 inch set, for partial-sun spaces.
products.description:
The Phonecessity L-100 is a weatherproof outdoor 86 inch 4K QNED smart TV, listed for partial-sun spaces. It is the only outdoor-rated set in the ranking, and the listing shows no price bracket.

It finishes last because it is a niche product. For a covered patio or poolside entertaining area it solves a problem the other six cannot, but almost every reader will want an indoor TV instead. The QNED panel and true 86 inch size are appealing, though the missing price and install details make it harder to judge.

Buy it if you have a covered outdoor space and want a screen that can live there. Skip it if you only need an indoor set. The listing says partial sun, so full direct sunlight is not stated as supported, and you should confirm that before buying.
products.skipIf: You only need an indoor TV.

whatMatters.detail: The 85 inch versus 86 inch question is mostly about the retail catalog. Consumer sets are sold as 85 inch, and true 86 inch panels are mostly commercial. The visible difference is about one inch. Check the exact size in the title, and pick by use, not by that inch.

Panel type describes the screen technology. QLED and QNED add quantum dot or similar color layers beyond a plain LED panel, which makes color richer. The Hisense E6 is the only QLED here. Look for the panel name in the title, since a generic LED label usually means the basic tier.

Consumer sets are built for living rooms, with streaming apps and gaming features. Commercial sets are built for signage and meeting rooms, with long run hours and fewer home extras. The two LG 86 inch panels are commercial. Check the listing for words like Commercial before you assume it suits home use.

A screen this large is about 75 inches wide, so room and wall fit matter before the purchase. You also need to get it through doorways and stairwells. Measure your wall, your entry points and your mount, and compare against the product dimensions listed in the specs.

Viewing distance sets how large a screen feels. An 85 inch 4K set suits roughly 9 to 12 feet away, and closer shows the pixel structure. Measure from your seat to the wall. If you sit nearer than 9 feet, consider whether a smaller panel would give a cleaner picture.

faq.q: Is there a true 86 inch consumer TV here?
faq.a: Not a consumer one. The true 86 inch sets here are the LG Commercial Lite, the LG PK340S and the outdoor Phonecessity. The consumer sets, like the Hisense E6 and Samsung U8000H, are 85 inch.
Insisting on 86 inches when an 85 inch set is nearly identical in size. The extra inch is invisible from the couch, and chasing it can push you toward a commercial display with fewer home features.

faq.q: Is QLED worth it over standard LED?
faq.a: If picture matters, yes. The Hisense E6 is QLED, which adds color technology over the plain LED panel on the Insignia F50. If you mostly watch casually, the Samsung U8000H is a simpler choice.

faq.q: How do I move an 85 inch TV?
faq.a: Plan for two people and check the box dimensions against your doorways, stairs and mount before delivery day. A set like the Samsung U8000H is wide at 85 inches, so clear a path and protect the screen face.

faq.q: Can the outdoor TV go in full sun?
faq.a: The listing for the Phonecessity says partial sun, so full direct sunlight is not stated as supported. It is meant for covered patios. Check the listing and the manual for install and weather requirements before you buy.

faq.q: Do commercial TVs work at home?
faq.a: They work as displays, but they have fewer home features. The LG Commercial Lite 86UR340C9UD lists smart TV functions, while the PK340S is aimed at meeting rooms. For a living room, a consumer set like the Hisense E6 fits better.

finalTake: For most homes, the Hisense 85E6QF is the best big TV here, thanks to its QLED panel. Samsung's U8000H is a safe brand pick, and LG's Nano model helps if audio matters. Choose the commercial LG panels only if you need exactly 86 inches for work, and keep the Phonecessity for covered outdoor spaces.
